॥ श्रीरस्तु ॥
प्रस्तावना.
वीरशैवलिंगिब्राह्मणहो, जगामध्यें वीरशैवमतानुसारी सर्व लोकांना निराभारी जंगमाचें लक्षण समजून घेणे अत्यावश्यक आहे परंतु निराभारी जंगमाचें लक्षण प्रतिपादणारे ग्रंथ अतिशय दुर्मिळ आहेत. आणि जंगमलक्षणबोधक ग्रंथ प्रसिद्ध करण्याविषयीं अनेक वीरशैवांनी सूचना केल्या आहेत, याकरितां श्रीमद्भुवनभवनारंभस्तंभायमान परशिवावतार निरंजन जंगमोत्पत्ति वगैरे विषयांनी भरलेले, सप्रमाण मानलेले, उत्तरवातुलतंत्र, सूक्ष्मागम, शंकरसंहिता, पारमेश्वरागम, सुप्रभेदागम, व्यासकृत भविष्यत्पुराणांतर्गत प्रभुलिंगलीला, सिद्धांतशिखामणि, अनादिवीरशैवसारसंग्रह, वीरशैवाचारप्रदीपिका वगैरे ग्रंथांतील जंगमाची उत्पत्ति, आचरण वगैरे विषय काढून ते विषय एकेठिकाणीं आणून " विरक्तोत्पत्तिक्रियालक्षण " नांवाचा हा ग्रंथ प्रसिद्ध केला आहे.
या ग्रंथांतील विषय त्या त्या ग्रंथांत जसजसे सांपडत गेले, तसतसें छापावयास दिल्यामुळे अनुक्रमानें विषय आले नाहींत तथापि वाचकांना सुलभरीतीनें विषय सांपडावेत ह्मणून अनुक्रमणिकेंत श्लोकाचे आंकडे दिले आहेत.
पुढच्या आवृत्तीच्या वेळेस अनुक्रमानें विषय आणून ग्रंथाची सुधारणा करूं.
या ग्रंथांचे प्रूफ तपास करणें वगैरे कामांत वे. मू. जगदीश शास्त्री नालवार वे. मू. मल्लिकार्जुनशास्त्री जैनापूर वे. शा. सं. रंगाचार्य शास्त्री मुधोळकर यांनीं मदत केली याबद्दल आह्मी यांचे आभारी आहों.
प्रसिद्धकर्ता
मणूरमठाध्यक्ष मल्लिकार्जुन शास्त्री
data.english:
॥ May there be auspiciousness ॥

Preface.

O Vīraśaiva Liṅgī Brāhmaṇas, in this world it is absolutely necessary for all people who follow the Vīraśaiva doctrine to understand the characteristics of the nirābhārī Jaṅgama. However, the texts that expound the characteristics of the nirābhārī Jaṅgama are extremely rare. Moreover, many Vīraśaivas have suggested that a text explaining the characteristics of the Jaṅgama should be published. Therefore, drawing from subjects such as the origin of the niranjana Jaṅgama—who is the incarnation of Parashiva and the foundational pillar beginning from the venerable Bhūvanabhāṭṭa—and supported with authoritative sources, materials have been compiled from texts like Uttara Vātula Tantra, Sūkṣmāgama, Śaṅkara Saṁhitā, Pārameśvarāgama, Suprabhedāgama, Vyāsa’s Bhaviṣyat Purāṇa (including Prabhuliṅga Līlā), Siddhānta Śikhāmaṇi, Anādi Vīraśaiva Sāra Saṅgraha, Vīraśaivācāra Pradīpikā, etc. Extracting the topics of the origin, conduct, and related aspects of the Jaṅgama from these works and bringing them together in one place, this book titled “Viraktotpatikriyālakṣaṇa” has been published.

Since the materials from these texts were sent for printing as and when they were found in their respective sources, the topics have not appeared in a sequential order. Nevertheless, in order to help readers easily locate the subjects, verse numbers have been provided in the index.

In the next edition, the subjects will be arranged sequentially and the text will be improved.

In the work of proofreading and related tasks for this book, assistance was provided by Vedamūrti Jagadīśa Śāstrī Nālvar, Vedamūrti Mallikārjuna Śāstrī Jaināpūr, and Vedashāstrasaṁpanna Raṅgācārya Śāstrī Mudhoḷkar. For this, we are grateful to them.

Publisher
Head of Maṇūr Maṭha, Mallikārjuna Śāstrī

॥ १ ॥ मंदर पर्वतावर सर्व गण एकत्र मिळून निष्कलंक अशा परमेश्वराची पुढे होणारी या संसारपाशापासून मुक्त करणारी लीला 
॥ २ ॥ समजून घेण्याच्या उद्देशानें परमेश्वरास प्रार्थना करिते  झाले, याप्रमाणें गणांनीं प्रार्थिलेले परमेश्वर लीलेने म्हणाले; कीः-
॥ ३ ॥ माझ्या मस्तकांतील चक्राच्या मध्यभागी, मोक्षदायक, निष्कलंक व प्रकाशमान निरंजन असें साक्षात् चरलिंग प्रकट झाले. 
॥ ४ ॥ हें माझें चरलिंग मजहून शंभरपट श्रेष्ठ होय. मी श्रेष्ठ अशा शक्तीने युक्त असा आहे परंतु हें चरलिंग शक्तीपासून अतीत आहे. 
॥ ५ ॥ मी कलांनीं युक्त आहे, पण हे चरलिंग कलाहीन आहे, मी वर्णानें युक्त आहे, पण हें चरलिंग वर्णापासून अतीत (वेगळे) असे आहे. 
॥ ६ ॥ या चरलिंगाला कृतयुगांत, निरंजन, त्रेतायुगांत, निर्माय, 
॥ ७ ॥ द्वापरयुगांत, निष्कल, व कलियुगांत प्रभु अशी क्रमानें नांव आली आहेत, 
॥ ८ ॥ कलियुगांत या प्रभुदेवाचे पीठ बसवेश्वरादि प्रमथांकडून कल्याण शहरी स्थापिले जाणार आहे. 
॥ ९ ॥ तें पीठ तीन चैतन्यांनी युक्त, तिन्हीं रूपें एकत्र जेथे झाली आहेत असें; नाद, बिंदु व कलामयः शून्यरूप; ओंकारात्मकः निर्गुण (गुण रहित); सर्वशून्य, तीन भेदांनी राहणारें असे आहे. 
॥ १० ॥ या पीठांत ओंकाराचे तीन भाग असल्यामुळे हें तीन भेदांनीं राहणारें असें म्हटलें आहे. याच कारणानें शून्य सिंहासन या नांदानें तें जगांत प्रसिद्ध आहे.
data.english:
This is the portion from the dialogue that took place between Pramathaganas and Śiva in the Uttara Vātula:

1. On Mount Mandara, all the gaṇas, having assembled together, prayed to the stainless Parameśvara with the intention of understanding the forthcoming divine play that liberates from the bondage of worldly existence.

2. Thus prayed by the gaṇas, Parameśvara, through His divine play, said:

3. “In the center of the chakra in My head, there manifested the directly perceptible Chara-Liṅga, which is liberating, stainless, radiant, and Niranjana.

4. This Chara-Liṅga of Mine is a hundred times superior to Me. I am endowed with supreme Śakti, but this Chara-Liṅga is beyond Śakti.

5. I am associated with kalās (aspects), but this Chara-Liṅga is without kalās. I possess varṇa (attributes/forms), but this Chara-Liṅga is beyond varṇa (distinct from all attributes).

6. This Chara-Liṅga is called Niranjana in Kṛta Yuga, Nirmāya in Tretā Yuga,

7. Niṣkala in Dvāpara Yuga, and in Kali Yuga it is known as Prabhu ( Allama prabhu/Prabhudeva ).

8. In Kali Yuga, the seat (pīṭha) of this Prabhudeva will be established in the city of Kalyāṇa by Basaveśvara and other Pramathas.

9. That pīṭha is endowed with three consciousnesses, where the three forms unite; it is constituted of Nāda, Bindu, and Kalā; it is of the nature of Śūnya; it is Omkāra itself; it is Nirguṇa (devoid of qualities); it is the absolute void, and exists in three distinctions.

10. Since this pīṭha contains the three parts of Omkāra, it is said to exist in three distinctions. For this very reason, it is well-known in the world by the name “Śūnya Siṁhāsana.”

॥ १६ ॥ या रीतीनें या मताचे पालन कर व लोकांचा उद्धार करण्यास्तव शिष्यसमूह वाढीव. 
॥ १७ ॥ याप्रमाणें आज्ञा केल्यानंतर त्तो भगवान् निरंजन प्रभु गणश्रेष्ठांनींयुक्त असा लोककल्याणास्तव पृथ्वीवर संचार करील 
॥ १८ ॥ भक्तांचीं पापें निवारण करण्याकरितां त्या भक्तांना दीक्षा व ज्ञानोपदेश देंऊन सर्व देशांत लोककल्याणास्तव 
॥ १९ ॥ माझ्या धर्माचा प्रसार करून तो पुनः मजकडे येईल. नंतर पृथ्वीवरील त्यांचे वंशज त्यानें सांगितल्याप्रमाणे वागणारे असे होऊन
||२०-२१|| भक्तांना अनुग्रह करण्यास्तव पृथ्वीवर संचार करून व जिकडे तिकडे मठ स्थापून व दीक्षादि संस्कार करून, माझ्या मताचा उद्धार करितील.
data.english:
11. The lord of the Pramatha gaṇas, that Bhagavān, being dependent upon devotees, went to the temple of the revered Basaveśvara and, sitting upon the seat,

12. bestowed, with grace, knowledge-initiation (jñāna-dīkṣā) upon Basaveśvara and the other gaṇas, and

13. clearly explained to those gaṇas the doctrine of Liṅgāṅga-sāmarasya, which embodies the essence of all Vedānta, and, removing all defects, granted them prasāda and other blessings,

14. thus purifying them; and there itself, seeing that there was the attainment of Ṣaṭsthala, he beheld the excellent and brahmacārī Śrī Channabasaveśvara,

15. and, casting a gracious glance upon him, called him near and gave him his own mudrā (seal), pīṭha (seat), and the book of ācāras (conduct),

16. saying, “In this manner, uphold this doctrine and increase the community of disciples for the upliftment of the people.”

17. After giving this command, that Bhagavān Niranjana Prabhu, accompanied by the foremost gaṇas, will move upon the earth for the welfare of the world,

18. and for the removal of the sins of devotees, he will grant initiation and impart knowledge to those devotees, and for the welfare of the people in all regions,

19. he will propagate My dharma and then return to Me. Thereafter, his descendants on earth, acting according to what he has taught,

20–21. will move upon the earth to bestow grace upon devotees, and, establishing maṭhas everywhere and performing initiatory rites and other samskaras (sacraments), will uplift My doctrine.

चित्रकलदुर्गचे निराभारी स्वामी यांची वंशावळ.
या कंलियुगांत शिवाचार मताचे मुख्य गुरु षट्स्थल ब्रह्मी षण्मुख स्वामी हे होत. यांचे मागून श्रीमन्महाराज निरंजन जगद्गुरु अल्लमप्रभु हे शून्य सिंहासनारूढ झाले.
॥१॥
चेन्नबसवण्ण स्वामी शून्य सिंहासनाचे पहिले अधिपति होऊन कांहीं दिवस राहिलें त्यांनी पुष्कळं महत्कृत्ये केलीं व नंतर ते उळवीस जाते झाले. यांचा उंळवी येथे असणारां मठच याला दृष्टांत होय.
॥२॥
.. दुसरी गादी तोंटद सिद्धेश्वरं स्वामी यांस मिळाली यांनींही अनेक महत्कृत्ये केलीं व शेवटीं यडूर येथे ते लिंगैक्य पावले. यडूर गांवींचं त्यांची समाधि आहे.
॥३॥
तिसरी गादीं निरक्षरबोळ बसवेश्वर स्वामी यांसं प्राप्त झाली. तोटद सिद्धेश्वर स्वामीच्या कृपेनें हे समस्त विद्यापारंगत असून यांनींही अनेक महत्वाचीं कृत्यें करून मुधुगिरी (मद्गिरी) येथे देह ठेविला येथे त्यांची समाधि आहे.
॥ ४ ॥
चौथी गादी सिद्ध‌वीरं स्वामी यांस मिळाली. यांची समाधिं गुम्मळापूर येथे आहे.
॥ ५ ॥
पांचवी गांदी सिद्धवीर स्वामी यांस मिळाली. यांची समाधि गुन्ळूर येथे आहे.
॥ ६ ॥
सहावी गादी गगनस्वामी यांस प्राप्त झाली. यांची समाधि भैरवाच्या दुर्गात आहे.
॥ ७ ॥
सातवी गादी कट्टिगेहल्ली स्वामी यांस मिळाली. यांची समाधि तिकुवल्ली येथे आहे.
|| ८ ||
आठवी गादी इम्मडि गुरिग्या राजेंद्र स्वामी यांस प्राप्त झाली. दिल्लीशहरास जाऊन यांनी शून्य सिंहासनाकरितां शिखाशैल आणून चित्रदुर्ग येथे मठ स्थापन करून अनेक महत्कार्ये करून तेथेच देह ठेविते झाले. यांची समाधि बृहन्मठांत आहे.
॥ ९ ॥
इम्मडि गुरुसिद्ध स्वामी यांस शिखापट्ट प्राप्त झाला यांची समाधि अनंतपूर येथे
॥ १०॥
स्वादीचे चेन्नबसव राजेंद्र स्वामी यांस शिखापट्ट मिळाला. यांची समाधि मागडी येथे आहे. 
॥ ११ ॥
data.english:
Lineage of the Nirābhārī Svāmīs of Chitrakaladurg.

1. In this Kali Yuga, the principal guru of the Śivācāra doctrine was Ṣaṭsthala Brahmī Ṣaṇmukha Svāmī. After him, the revered Niranjana Jagadguru Allamaprabhu ascended the Śūnya Siṁhāsana.

2. Chennabasavaṇṇa Svāmī became the first head of the Śūnya Siṁhāsana and remained for some time. He performed many great deeds and later went to Ulavi. The maṭha existing at Ulavi is evidence of this.

3. The second seat (gādī) was obtained by Toṇṭada Siddheśvara Svāmī. He also performed many great deeds and finally attained liṅgaikya at Yedur. His samādhi is in the village of Yedur.

4. The third seat was attained by Nirakṣarabola Basaveśvara Svāmī. By the grace of Toṇṭada Siddheśvara Svāmī, he became proficient in all knowledge. He too performed many important deeds and left his body at Mudhugiri (Madgiri). His samādhi is there.

5. The fourth seat was obtained by Siddhavīra Svāmī. His samādhi is at Gummalāpūr.

6. The fifth seat was obtained by Siddhavīra Svāmī. His samādhi is at Guṇḷūr.

7. The sixth seat was attained by Gaganasvāmī. His samādhi is in the fort of Bhairava.

8. The seventh seat was obtained by Kaṭṭigehalli Svāmī. His samādhi is at Tikuvalli.

9. The eighth seat was attained by Immaḍi Gurigya Rājendra Svāmī. He went to the city of Delhi and brought Śikhāśaila for the Śūnya Siṁhāsana, established a maṭha at Chitradurga, performed many great works, and left his body there. His samādhi is in the Bṛhanmaṭha.

10. Immaḍi Gurusiddha Svāmī obtained the Śikhāpaṭṭa. His samādhi is at Anantapur.

11. Svādi’s Chennabasava Rājendra Svāmī obtained the Śikhāpaṭṭa. His samādhi is at Magadi.

वप्पोत्तिन चनवीर स्वामी यांस शिखापट्ट झाला यांची समाधि तिकुवल्ली येथे आहे.
॥ १६ ॥
व्याकरण सिद्धलिंगस्वामी यांस शिखापट्ट झाला यांची समाधि मागडि येथे आहे.
॥ १७ ॥
नैघंटचे सिद्धबसव स्वामी यांस शिखापट्ट यांची समाधि हावेरी येथे आहे.
॥ १८ ॥
सण्णवरचे राचोटी स्वामी यांस शिखापट्ट यांची समाधि चिन्मूलादि येथे.
॥ १९ ॥
सावळगीचे गुरुशांत स्वामी यांस शिखापट्ट यांची समाधि चिन्मूलादि येथे
॥ २० ॥
सण्णपाद चेन्नवीर स्वामी यांस शिखापट्ट यांची समाधि चित्रदुर्गच्या बृहन्मठांत आहे.
॥ २१ ॥
कलिवर्ष ४९६३, शालिवाहन शक १७८४, दुंदुभिनामसंवत्सर फाल्गुन शुद्ध
५ मी भानुवार या दिवशीं महालिंग स्वामी यांस शिखापट्ट झाला. यांची समाधि शिरसंगी येथे आहे.
॥ २२ ॥
रुद्रस्वामी यांस शिखापट्ट झाला, यांची समाधि चिन्मूलाद्रि येथील बृहन्मठांत आहे.
॥ २३ ॥
मुप्पिनस्वामी यांस शिखापद्द झाला.
ही वरील माहिती चित्रकलदुर्ग शून्यसिंहासनाधीश जगद्‌गुरु मूरिग्याराजेंद्र महास्वामी यांच्या मठांतील दाखल्यावरून संक्षिप्तरूपानें घेतलेली आहे,
: याप्रमाणें आजपर्यंत वंश चालत आला. प्रत्येक स्वामीचे चरित्र कितीही संक्षिप्तरूपानें दिलें तरी वाढणारच, याकरितां प्रत्येकाचें नांव, मूलस्थान व समाधीची जागा मात्र यांत दिलेली आहे.

निराभारिलक्षणं.
सूक्ष्मागमे, १२ पटले.

निराभारी यांचीं लक्षणें.
।। १ ।। निराभारी चरमूर्ति (विरक्त लोक) यांना सहा गुण भूषणास्पद आहेत. त्यांत एक गुण जर कमी असला तर संसारी लोकांमध्ये त्यांची गणना होते 
॥ २ ॥ हे सहा गुण कोणते तरः-१ वैराग्य, २ ज्ञान, ३ ब्रह्मचर्य, ४ तप, ५ करुणा, ६ सदाचार. यांना षड्गुण असें ह्मणतात 
॥ ३ ।। हे सहा संस्कारगुण जो लिंगधारी चरन्ती टाकितो तो सदाचारी नव्हे. तो चरंती प्रत्यक्ष राक्षस मानावा 
॥ ४ ॥ जो चरन्ती लिंगीब्राह्मणाचे पोटी जन्मून, लिंग धारण करून शास्त्रोक्त कर्मे आचरितो व कामनीरहित असतो, तो चरन्ती " निराभारी " ही पदवी पावतो. 
॥ ५ ॥ जो चरन्ती वीरशैव मतानें वागतो व लिंगधारण करितो, पण जर तो चरन्ती संचार न करितां अन्नग्रहण करितो, तो चरन्ती " वीरशैव " कसा बरें होईल? 
॥ ६ ॥ हे महादेवि पार्वति, सर्वभक्त सदाचारवृत्तीमध्ये जर दक्ष होऊन वागतील तर त्यांचेपासून "चरमूर्ति " निपजणार नाहींत काय? 
॥७॥ त्या चरमूर्तीपासून ज्ञान संपादन करून, शाप देण्याचे, दान देण्याचे, व दुसऱ्यास दया दाखविण्याचे सामर्थ्य ज्यांमध्ये आहे असे ज्ञानी उत्तम भक्त या वीरमार्गात निष्णात असे निर्माण होणार नाहींत काय ? 
॥८॥ जो चरन्ती सदाचारी तोच वीर तोच वीरशैव मताचा होय. जो चरन्ती श्रेष्ठ असून अनाचारी असेल तर त्यास गणश्रेष्ठांनी निंद्य मानणे योग्य आहे

Nirābhāri-lakṣaṇam (Characteristics of the Nirābhāri Virasaiva)
From Sūkṣmāgama, Chapter 12

1. The Nirābhāri, who are the supreme ascetic forms (detached beings), are adorned with six virtues. If even one of these virtues is lacking, they are to be counted among worldly people.

2. These six virtues are: (1) detachment (vairāgya), (2) knowledge (jñāna), (3) celibacy (brahmacharya), (4) austerity (tapas), (5) compassion (karuṇā), and (6) righteous conduct (sadācāra). These are called the six qualities (ṣaḍguṇa).

3. One who abandons these six cultivated virtues, even if bearing the linga, is not righteous; such a person should be regarded as truly demonic.

4. One who is born in a lineage of linga-bearing Brahmins, who wears the linga, performs scripturally prescribed duties, and remains free from desire—such a one attains the title “Nirābhāri.”

5. One who follows the Vīraśaiva doctrine and wears the linga, but eats without undertaking proper wandering (discipline), how can such a person truly be called a Vīraśaiva?

6. O great goddess Pārvatī, if all devotees conduct themselves diligently in righteous behavior, will not supreme beings (charamūrtis) arise from among them?

7. From such exalted beings, will there not emerge learned and excellent devotees in this heroic path—endowed with the power to acquire knowledge, grant blessings, give charity, and show compassion to others?

8. One who is righteous alone is truly a Vīra, and indeed a follower of the Vīraśaiva doctrine. If one is outwardly great but unrighteous, it is proper that the noble regard him as condemnable.

।। ९ ।। अनाचारामध्यें आसक्ति ठेविल्यानें मोठीं पापें उद्भवतात व पापांपासून तो चरन्ती यातनेला पात्र होतो 
।।१०।। अज्ञानापासून, रागापासून, अगर मोहापासून मनुष्य पातकें करितात व त्यामुळे त्यांस यातना भोगाव्या लागतात 
॥ ११ ॥ निराभारी यांनी व वीरशैव भक्तांनी आपल्या इष्ट लिंगास काषायवस्त्र भूषण करावें
॥ १२ ॥ माझ्या ध्यानीं रत अशा भक्तांना पांढरें शिवसूत्र, पांढर लिंगवस्त्र, पांढरीं प्रावरणें दोषास्पद होत असें मानावें 
॥ १३ ॥ हे पार्वति, लोकांमध्यें पूज्य व विरक्त अशा निराभारी चरन्तीनें काषायवस्त्र सोडून पांढरें वस्त्र धारण करूं नये 
॥ १४ ॥ ज्ञाना मध्ये कृमिकीटकांपेक्षां पशु श्रेष्ठ; पशूपेक्षां मनुष्यें श्रेष्ठ; मनुष्यांमध्ये द्विज (ब्राह्मण, क्षत्रिय, वैश्य) श्रेष्ठ; 
।। १५ ।। द्विजांमध्यें ब्राह्मण श्रेष्ठ; ब्राह्मणांत यज्ञ करूं इच्छिणारे ब्राह्मण श्रेष्ठ. त्यांहून खरोखर यज्ञ करणारे श्रेष्ठ, आणि त्यांहून सन्यासी श्रेष्ठ 
॥ १६ ॥ संन्याशांहून ज्ञानी श्रेष्ठ; ज्ञान्यांमध्ये शंकराची पूजा करणारे ज्ञानी श्रेष्ठ; आणि हे महाभाग, शंकराची पूजा करणाऱ्यांमध्ये माझे लिंग अंगावर धारण करून पूजा करणारे श्रेष्ठ 
॥१७॥ लिंग धारण करणाऱ्यांमध्यें षट्स्थल जाणणारा श्रेष्ठ; त्याहून श्रेष्ठ पुरुष या त्रैलोक्यांत कधीही असू शकणार नाहीं 
।। १८ ।। संसार जिंकूं इच्छिणाऱ्या लोकांनी या षट्स्थल जाणणाऱ्या श्रेष्ठ पुरुषांस नेहमीं वंदन करावें व त्याचे पूजन करावें. फार काय सांगावें ? हे वत्सा, तोच हा असें जाण; यांत कांहीं संशय नाहीं.

9. Attachment to unrighteous conduct gives rise to great sins, and through such sins one becomes subject to suffering.

10. From ignorance, attachment, or delusion, people commit sins and must consequently endure suffering.

11. The Nirābhāri and Vīraśaiva devotees should adorn their iṣṭa-liṅga with saffron-colored cloth.

12. Devotees absorbed in my meditation should regard white sacred threads, white linga-cloths, and white garments as improper).

13. O Pārvatī, a Nirābhāri ascetic—honored and detached among people—should not abandon saffron garments to wear white clothing.

14. In the hierarchy of beings: animals are superior to worms and insects; humans are superior to animals; among humans, the twice-born (Brāhmaṇa, Kṣatriya, Vaiśya) are superior.

15. Among the twice-born, Brāhmaṇas are superior; among Brāhmaṇas, those who desire to perform sacrifices are superior; greater still are those who actually perform sacrifices; and superior even to them are renunciates (sannyāsins).

16. Superior to renunciates are the enlightened; among the enlightened, those who worship Śaṅkara are superior; and among such worshippers, those who wear and worship the linga upon their body are the highest.

17. Among those who wear the linga, the one who knows the doctrine of the six stages (ṣaṭsthala) is the highest; beyond such a person, none greater can exist in the three worlds.

18. Those who seek to conquer worldly existence should always bow to and worship such a knower of ṣaṭsthala. What more need be said? O child, know that he alone is the supreme—there is no doubt in this.

॥ १९ ॥ याप्रमाणें सुयशावल्लभानें (नंदी ने) पूर्वी कुमारास ( कार्तिकेयास ) संतोषानें जी एक गोष्ट सांगितली तीच, हे पार्वति, मी तुला आतां एथें सांगितली 
॥ २० ॥ ज्यास्थळीं वीरशैव क्षणक्षणीं विराजमान होतो तें स्थळ लिंगाचे घर ह्मणून निश्चयेंकरून जाण 
॥ २१ ॥ हे देवि, वीरशैवाचे उदरीं जन्मलेला निराभारी महेश्वर होय; व वीरशैव असा जो त्याचा बाप तो गणेश्वर होय 
।। २२ ॥ वीरशैव हा पितारूप, मातारूप व गुरुरूप असून निरंजन लिंगरूप असा आहे 
॥ २३ ॥ गुरुश्रेष्ठ, निगमागम शिकविणारा असा जो निराभारी तो भक्तिकारण वैभवाच्या योगानें पश्चिमस्थानगलित झालेला आहे 
॥२४॥ लोकांस पावन करणारी भागीरथीही त्याच्या पादकमलापासून उद्भवली, ती गंगानदी वीरशैवाच्या गळ्यांतील माळ बनली 
॥२५॥ हे देवि, मी क्रियाहीन, तसाच लिंगहीन व आकारहीन होत्साता केवल ज्ञानरूपानें संचार करितों 
।। २६।। देवि, माझा भक्त, वीरशैववान्, देहधारी, लिंगधारी व क्रिया आणि ज्ञान यांनीं युक्त असा संचार करितो 
।।२७।। सर्वांमध्ये मी श्रेष्ठ; पण वीरशैव माझे यजमान होत; हे देवि, त्यांच्यांहून कोणी श्रेष्ठ नाहीं, हीगोष्ट अगदीं खरी आहे यांत कांहीं संशय नाहीं 
॥२८॥  हे प्रिये, ज्या निराभारी चरन्तीमध्ये अनाचार आढळतो (जो निराभारी अनाचाराने वागतो) तो माझ्या वचनेंकरून (आज्ञेनें) अधम मानिला जातो 
।।२९॥ शुद्ध अशा वर्तनानें सर्व धर्मास गंभीरपणा प्राप्त होतो, दुर्वर्तनानें सर्व धर्म लयास जातो.

19. Thus, the teaching that was once joyfully spoken by Suyaśavallabha (Nandī) to Kumāra (Kārtikeya), that same teaching, O Pārvatī, I have now told you here.

20. Wherever a Vīraśaiva resides, that place should certainly be known as the abode of the linga.

21. O goddess, one born from the womb of a Vīraśaiva is a Nirābhāri Maheśvara; and the Vīraśaiva who is his father is a Gaṇeśvara.

22. The Vīraśaiva is father, mother, and guru; and is of the nature of the stainless linga itself.

23. That Nirābhāri who is the supreme guru and teacher of the Nigama and Āgama has, through the power of devotion, transcended worldly states.

24. Even the purifying river Bhāgīrathī arose from his lotus feet; that Ganges becomes a garland around the neck of the Vīraśaiva.

25. O goddess, I, being without action, without linga, and without form, move about purely as knowledge itself.

26. O goddess, my devotee, the Vīraśaiva, moves about embodied, bearing the linga, and endowed with both action and knowledge.

27. Among all, I am supreme; yet the Vīraśaiva is my master. O goddess, none is superior to them—this is absolutely true, without doubt.

28. O beloved, a Nirābhāri ascetic in whom unrighteous conduct is found is, by my command, to be regarded as base.

29. Through pure conduct all dharma attains gravity and strength; through misconduct all dharma is destroyed.

शंकरसंहितायां, अध्याय ८३

॥५१॥ निराभारी यानें समानबुद्धि (सर्व प्राण्याविषयीं) रूप कंथा, क्षमारूप विभूतीचा गोळा, दयारूप कमंडलु, सत्यज्ञानरूप मनोहर दंड हीं धारण करावीं 
॥५२॥ वैराग्यरूप भिक्षापात्र घेऊन, शुद्ध व सदाचारी अशा लिंगधारी लोकांपाशीं भक्तिरूप भिक्षा मागावी 
॥५३॥ याप्रमाणे संचार करणारा जो निराभारी त्यास पुढे सांगितलेला कुटुंबपरिंवार प्राप्त होतो - विद्या स्त्री, संतोष पुत्र, क्षमा दासी, 
।।५४।। भक्ति आई, सदाचार बाप, सत्य नातू, शम मित्र, वैराग्य उदार स्नेही, दम आचार्य (गुरु), श्रद्धा (विश्वास) बहीण, 
॥५५॥ अहिंसा दासी, चोरी न करणें हा गुण दास मानिला आहे, मैत्र्यादि गुण लेकरें, धर्म वाहन मानिलें आहे. 
॥५६॥ ज्ञानरूप शरीर, सर्व गोचरविचाररूपी क्षेत्र, मोक्षरूपी स्थान, जेथें प्राणलिंग धारण करणाऱ्यास सहज जातां येतें 
॥५७।। हे वत्सा, याप्रमाणें बरोबर परिवार घेऊन शुद्ध परिपूर्ण व चिदानंदी होत्साता या भूमीवर संचार कर..

अध्याय ८१

॥ ४८ ॥ सर्व आश्रमातीत असा प्राणलिंगधारी यानें विभूतीचा गोळा, कंथा, क-मंडलु, भिक्षापात्र व दंड धारण करावा 
।। ४९ ॥ या पांच महामुद्रा (कंथा, कमंडलु, वगैरे) ज्या ज्या मनुष्यामध्ये असतात त्या त्या मनुष्याला शरण जाऊन पूर्ण अशा भक्तीनें त्याचे पूजन करावें. 
॥ ५० ॥ हे वत्सा, या पांच मुद्रांनी युक्त असा धर्म ज्यांत प्रवर्ततो (विशेष करून वसतो) तो मनुष्य प्राणलिंग धारण करणाऱ्यांस नेहमीं वंद्य व पूज्य होतो.

From Śaṅkara Saṁhitā, Chapter 83

51. A Nirābhāri should wear: a cloak in the form of equal-mindedness (towards all beings), sacred ash in the form of forgiveness, a water-pot in the form of compassion, and a staff in the form of true knowledge.

52. Taking a begging bowl in the form of detachment, he should seek alms in the form of devotion from pure and righteous linga-bearers.

53. The Nirābhāri who lives in this manner attains the following family: knowledge as his wife, contentment as his son, and forgiveness as his servant.

54. Devotion is his mother, righteous conduct his father, truth his grandson, tranquility his friend, detachment his generous companion, self-restraint his teacher (guru), and faith his sister.

55. Non-violence is his maidservant; non-stealing is regarded as his servant; virtues such as friendliness are his children; and dharma is considered his vehicle.

56. His body is knowledge, the field is all objects of perception and thought, and liberation is his abode—where one who bears the prāṇa-liṅga can easily reach.

57. O child, thus moving about on this earth with such a family, he becomes pure, complete, and full of consciousness and bliss.

Chapter 81

48. One who bears the prāṇa-liṅga and transcends all āśramas should carry sacred ash, a cloak, a water-pot, a begging bowl, and a staff.

49. Whoever possesses these five great marks (cloak, water-pot, etc.), one should surrender to such a person and worship him with complete devotion.

50. O child, a person in whom this dharma—endowed with these five marks—resides is always worthy of reverence and worship for those who bear the prāṇa-liṅga.

॥ ७५ ॥ निराभार मताविषयी सांगतों, लक्षपूर्वक ऐक 
॥ ७६ ॥ प्राण्यांचे पुण्य व पाप असे दोन प्रकारचें कर्म आहे. अशा कर्माच्या भारापासून निवृत्त झालेला (कर्मबंधनांपासून मुक्त) असा जो तो निराभारी मानिला जातो. 
॥ ७७ ॥ जटाधारी किंवा मुंडन करणारा अथवा शिखा राखणारा, काषाय वस्त्र परिधान करणारा, निस्पृह, निजलिंगामध्यें ऐक्य पावलेला, भिक्षान्न भोजन करणारा, निर्भय 
॥ ७८ ॥ मौन धारण करणारा, प्राणिमात्रांवर दया दाखविणारा, असा जो तो निराभारी मानिला आहे. जटाधारी यांचे माहात्म्य ज्या प्रकारचें त्या प्रकारचेच माहात्म्य मुंडन करणाऱ्यांचेही होय 
॥ ७९ ॥ कंथा, कमंडलु, विभूति, रुद्राक्ष, दंड व कौपीन धारण करणारा निराभारी मानिला जातो 
॥ ८० ॥ काम-क्रोधरहित, शिवज्ञानी व जितेंद्रिय असा होत्साता त्यानें वनांतील पत्रांनीं, पुष्पांनी व फलांनीं लिंगाचे पूजन करावें 
॥ ८१ ॥ पर्यटन करणाऱ्या जंगमानें दयायुक्त होऊन आपले पोट भरण्यापुरती मधुकरी भिक्षा मागावी 
॥ ८२ ॥ देवि, त्यानें एकाच घरचें अन्न जेऊं नये, तें दोषास्पद आहे. हे पार्वति, मधुकर (भोंगा) जसा फुलांपासून मधुर रस काढून घेतो, 
॥ ८३ ॥ त्याप्रमाणें त्यानें गृहस्थापाशी जाऊन भिक्षा मागावी. असें करणें उपवास करण्यासमान आहे. अथवा सद्गृहस्थांनी आदरपूर्वक बोलाविले असतां त्यांच्या घरीं एकान्न घेण्यास ह्मणजे जेवण करण्यासही हरकत नाहीं 
।। ८४ ।। भक्तिमान् सद्गृहस्थांनी या महेश्वरांचे ( या महात्म्या जंगमांचें) पूजन करणें योग्य आहे. यांना सोडून केलेली पूजा या लोकी निष्फल होते 
।। ८५ || जंगमानें वस्तुसंग्रह कोठेही करून ठेऊं नये; आपणास मिळालेलें दान त्यानें दयायुक्त होऊन गरीब अशा भक्तांस देऊन टाकावें

From Sūkṣmāgama, Chapter 7

75. I shall explain the doctrine of Nirābhāri—listen attentively.

76. There are two types of karma: merit and sin. One who is freed from the burden of such karma (liberated from bondage) is called Nirābhāri.

77. Whether one has matted hair, shaven head, or keeps a tuft; wears saffron garments; is desireless; united with one’s own linga; lives on alms; and is fearless—

78. maintains silence and shows compassion to all beings—such a person is called Nirābhāri. The greatness of those with matted hair is the same as that of those who shave their heads.

79. One who wears a cloak, water-pot, sacred ash, rudrākṣa beads, a staff, and a loincloth is considered Nirābhāri.

80. Free from lust and anger, endowed with knowledge of Śiva, and self-controlled, he should worship the linga with leaves, flowers, and fruits from the forest.

81. A wandering ascetic (jaṅgama), with compassion, should seek alms (madhukari) only for sustaining his body.

82. O goddess, he should not eat food from a single household; that improper. O Pārvatī, just as a bee gathers nectar from flowers—

83. in the same way he should seek alms from householders. Doing so is equal to fasting. However, if invited respectfully by a noble householder, he may partake of a full meal there.

84. Devout householders should worship such great souls (jaṅgamas). Worship performed without them becomes fruitless in this world.

85. A jaṅgama should not accumulate possessions; whatever he receives in charity should be compassionately given to poor devotees.

॥ ८६ ॥ आश्रमातीत अशा जंगमानें सुवर्ण, रत्न, वगैरे दान दिलेल्या वस्तूंचा संग्रह करून उपजीविका केली असतां तो पापी लोकांमध्ये श्रेष्ठ असा गणिला जातो 
॥ ८७ ॥ जो जटाधारी, शिखा राखिलेला अथवा मुंडन करणारा असून पांच मुद्रांनी युक्त होत्साता स्त्रीसंग करितो, तो खरोखर माझा द्रोही बनतो 
॥ ८८ ।। सर्व आश्रमातीत अशा प्राणलिंगधारण करणाऱ्या मुंडीनें (मुंडन करून घेणाऱ्यानें ) डोक्यास वस्त्र गुंडालू नये. अगर पागोटें घालू नये 
॥ ८९ ॥ ज्याप्रमाणें छिन्न भिन्न झालेलें अगर दुसऱ्या कोणत्याही दोषानें युक्त असें लिंग पूजण्यास अयोग्य मानिलें आहे त्याप्रमाणें लिंगाचारव्रतांप्रासून भ्रष्ट झालेला जंगम पूजण्यास अयोग्य होय.
॥ ९० ॥ या जंगमांनींही परस्परांस (एकमेकांस) हा शिव आहे अशा भावानें वंदन करावें. जो जंगम दुसऱ्या जंगमास पाहून त्यास वंदन करीत नाहीं 
॥ ९१ ॥ तो खरोखर जंगमद्वेषी व माझा द्वेषी होतो. हे पार्वति, जो अज्ञानानें जंगमाचा द्वेष करितो तो माझाच द्वेष करितो असें समजावे

।। ९३ ।। शिवाचें लिंगपूजन करण्याविषयीं श्रद्धा (भक्ति), इतर वृत्तींचें निरोधन करणें (स्तर वृत्ती दाबून टाकणें) हे धर्म ज्यामध्ये असतात तो भाराभारवर्जित (निराभारी) असा होतो 
।। ९४ ।। षट् (सहा) स्थलांविषयीं ज्ञान असणारा, सहा अंगांनी युक्त अशा
शरीराची समाधि करणारा, आपल्या प्रमाणे इतरांस जाणणारा असा जो तो निःसंशयेंकरून मीच आहे असें जाण 
।। ९५ ॥ हे पार्वति, वीरशैव मतामध्यें तत्पर असा मनुष्य जेथें राहातो तेंच तीर्थ, तेंच तप, शान्ति तेथेंच असते, मी तेथेंच नेहमीं राहतो 
॥ ९६ ॥ हे पार्वति, अशा लोकांना (वीरशैवमतामध्यें तत्पर अशा लोकांना) तीर्थयात्रेकरितां दुसरीकडे जाण्याची गरज नाहीं. लिंगधारण करणाऱ्यानें कैलासपद वगैरे मिळविण्याची इच्छा सोडून द्यावी

86. If such an ascetic collects wealth like gold and jewels and lives off it, he is considered foremost among sinners.

87. One who, though bearing marks like matted hair or shaven head and possessing the five symbols, engages in relations with women becomes truly a betrayer.

88. One who has renounced all āśramas and bears the prāṇa-liṅga should not cover the head with cloth or wear a turban.

89. Just as a broken or defective linga is unfit for worship, similarly a jaṅgama who has fallen from the observance of linga-discipline is unworthy of worship.

90. These jaṅgamas should greet each other with the awareness that “this is Śiva.” One who does not bow to another jaṅgama—

91. is truly a hater of jaṅgamas and a hater of me. O Pārvatī, one who ignorantly hates a jaṅgama is to be understood as hating me.

92. Therefore, those who live as jaṅgamas should regard one another as worthy of worship. Devotion to Śiva, knowledge of Śiva, Śiva’s marks, Śiva’s vows—

93. faith in worshipping the linga, and restraint of other tendencies—one in whom these qualities exist becomes free from all burdens (Nirābhāri).

94. One who knows the six stages (ṣaṭsthala), who meditates upon the body endowed with six limbs, and who sees others as oneself—know for certain that such a person is indeed myself.

95. O Pārvatī, wherever a person devoted to the Vīraśaiva doctrine resides, that place itself is a sacred pilgrimage, austerity, and peace—I dwell there always.

96. O Pārvatī, such people have no need to go elsewhere for pilgrimage. One who bears the linga should abandon the desire for attaining Kailāsa or other such states.

97. A linga-bearer should abandon places where deities other than Śiva are worshipped and should not seek the shelter of those who lack devotion to Śiva.

98. The giver, the receiver, and the object of charity should all be marked with the signs of Śiva. Only that which bears Śiva’s mark is fit to be given; all else is like the filth of an outcaste.

99. For devotees who wear the linga, there is no consideration of lunar dates, constellations, astrological combinations, or physiognomy.

100. One should see everything as pervaded by Śiva, with no sense of duality. Knowledge of objects united through the relation of linga and body is the means to liberation.

101. For those who bear my linga, that itself is liberation; therefore, all should always worship the linga with reverence.

From Pārameśvarāgama, Chapter 8

Īśvara says:

1. O goddess, what you ask about—the greatness and secret of my doctrine—I shall explain in detail; listen.

2. Among all deities, O Pārvatī, just as a warrior is called a hero in battle, similarly a person becomes a “Vīra” through noble devotion and firm detachment.

3. Those Śivayogis who are free from the three desires (for wealth, spouse, and offspring), devoted to knowledge and realization, and endowed with firm detachment are called Vīras.

4. O goddess, those linga-bearing Śivayogis who, though young and intelligent, are blind to the beauty of another’s wife are Vīras.

॥ ५ ॥ जे लिंगधारी शिवयोगी सर्व जाणणारे व वक्ते (बोलण्यांत चतुर) असे असून दुसऱ्यांचे दोष काढण्याच्या संबंधानें मुके असतात, ते वीर होत 
॥ ६ ॥ जे शिवयोगी परस्त्रीविषयीं षंढ (नपुंसक), दुसऱ्यास त्रास देण्याविषयीं पंगु (अवयवहीन), पदार्थांची रुचि घेण्याविषयीं जे जीभरहित असे असतात, ते वीर होत 
॥ ७ ॥ जे शिवयोगी अभिमान व दंभरहित असे असून अहिंसा, क्षमा व नम्रत्व यांनीं युक्त, आणि गुरुसेवेमध्यें तत्पर असतात ते वीर म्हणवितात 
॥ ८ ॥ शुचिर्भूतपणा (शुद्धाचरण) व आत्मनिग्रह (आपले मन आपल्या ता-ब्यांत ठेवणें ) करण्यामध्ये स्थिरत्व यांनी युक्त असून जे शिवयोगी अभिमानरहित व सर्वं ठिकाणीं समचित्त असे असतात, ते वीर होत.

।। १३ ।। सत्यव्रत आणि सत्य भाषण यांविषयीं आसक्ति असणारे, चोरीनें नव्हे पण चांगल्या रीतीनें मिळविलेल्या धनाचा उपभोग घेणारे, व कोणत्याही गोष्टीविषयी जास्त लंपट नसणें हा ज्यांचा स्वभावगुणच असे जे शिवयोगी ते वीर होत 
॥ १४ ॥ आपल्याहून जे श्रेष्ठ त्यांचा द्वेष न करणारे, आपल्या बरोबरीच्या लोकांचा मत्सर (हेवा) न करणारे व आपल्याहून कमी प्रतीच्या लोकांचा धिक्कार न करणार असे जे शिवयोगी ते वीर होत 
॥ १५ ॥ स्पर्धा, तिरस्कार व मत्सररहित असून शांत मनाचे व नेहमी माझ्या ध्यानामध्यें रत असणारे शिवयोगी वीर होत.
॥ १८ ॥ हे देवि, निजलेल्या वीरशैवानें उठतांच शिवरूपी गुरूचें ध्यान केलें तरी उठल्यावर लिंगरूपी गुरु जो मी त्या माझें ध्यान करावें 
।। १९ ।। सर्व देवतांमध्ये श्रेष्ठ, हे पार्वति, पर्ने, फुले व अक्षता जेवढ्या पूर्वदिवशी मिळतील तेवढ्या मिळवून ठेऊन त्यांच्या योगें करून सर्वदा उषःकाली (मोठ्या पहांटेस) पूजा करावी 
॥ २० ॥ हे पार्वति नित्य उषःकाली, मध्यान्ह काली व सायंकाळीं पूजन करावें. संध्याकाळीं व प्रातःकाळीं पूजन करण्याचे सामर्थ्य नसल्यास नेहमीं उषःकालीं पूजन करावें

5. Those who are knowledgeable and eloquent, yet remain mute when it comes to finding faults in others, are Vīras.

6. Those who are like eunuchs regarding others’ wives, lame in causing harm to others, and without taste for worldly objects are Vīras.

7. Those free from pride and hypocrisy, endowed with non-violence, forgiveness, humility, and devoted to serving the guru are called Vīras.

8. Those who are steadfast in purity and self-control, free from ego, and maintain equanimity everywhere are Vīras.

13. Those who are devoted to truth and truthful speech, who enjoy wealth earned righteously (not by theft), and are not excessively attached to anything—such Śivayogis are Vīras.

14. Those who do not hate those superior to them, do not envy equals, and do not despise those inferior—such Śivayogis are Vīras.

15. Those free from rivalry, contempt, and jealousy, calm in mind, and always absorbed in my meditation are Vīras.

18. O goddess, upon waking, a Vīraśaiva should meditate on the guru in the form of Śiva; thereafter, he should meditate on me, the guru in the form of the linga.

19. O Pārvatī, gathering leaves, flowers, and sacred rice from the previous day, one should perform worship early at dawn.

20. O Pārvatī, worship should be performed daily at dawn, midday, and evening. If unable to do all, at least perform it at dawn.

॥ २१ ॥ हे पार्वति, उषःकाळी पूजण्याचे सामर्थ्य असल्यास पूजन करावें, नाहींतर नित्य संध्याकाळीं पूजन करावें. जसें आपल्यास आवडतें तसें करावें ।। २२ ।। दररोज त्रिकाळ पूजा नेमानें करावीं; (तसें होत नसल्यास) मध्यान्हीं? तसी इच्छा नसल्यास, सायंकाळीं, व सकाळीं पूजन करावें. तेंही होत नसल्यास, हे पार्वति, एकदां तरी पूजन न चुकतां करावें 
॥२३॥ शक्ति व सहाय्य नसणाऱ्या मनुष्यानें नेहमी आपल्या इच्छेप्रमाणें पूजन करावें; सामर्थ्य असून जो पूजन करीत नाहीं तो रौरव नांवाच्या नरकांत पडतो.
।।२४।॥ माझें पूजनाची सामग्री असून व पूजन करण्याची शक्ति असून जो कामुक होऊन, विषयासक्त होऊन, ठकपणानें पूजन करीत नाहीं 
॥२५॥ तो कर्म व ज्ञान या दोहोंपासून पतित होत्साता दुःखसागरामध्ये बुडून जाऊन, चंद्र व नक्षत्रे आहेत तोपर्यंत रौरव नामक भयंकर नरकांत पडून राहतो 
॥२६॥ सूर्योदयाच्या पूर्वी दोन घटका जो काळ तो उषःकाल म्हंटला जातो; तोच शिवत्व प्राप्त करून देणारा पूजासमय होय 
॥ २७ ॥ अथवा सूर्योदयानंतर, मध्यान्हसमयीं तसेंच संध्याकाळी नक्षत्रांचे दर्शन झाल्यावरही पूजन करावें 
॥ २८ ॥ हे प्रिये, उषःकालची पूजा, जप, स्तोत्र वगैरे आटोपून गुरूला नमस्कार करून भिक्षेकरितां हिंडण्यास निघावें 
॥ ३० ॥ पक्क असो अथवा अपक भिक्षा असो ती आपल्यास पाहिजे तेवढी मागण्याकरितां फक्त लिंगधारी शिवयोगी चे घरी जावें 
॥ ३१ ॥ पादघंटा अथवा जयघंटा बांधून घेऊन, अथवा शंख व शिंग यांच्या नादेंकरून अथवा आपल्या दंडास (हातांतील काठीस) घंटा टांगून घेऊन भिक्षेकरितां हिंडण्यास जावें 
।। ३५ ।। रुद्राक्षांच्या मालांनीं, कंथा व कांबळ यांनी भूषित होऊन, कोणत्याही शब्दाच्या संज्ञेनें (खुणेनें) आपण आल्याबद्दल घरच्या लोकांस कळवून 
॥ ३३ ॥ लिंगधारी यानें सापल्या गुरुधर्माची आठवण करून "भिक्षा द्या" अशी घरच्या लोकांस आज्ञा करावी. घरच्या यजमानानें अथवा यजमानिणाने त्याः जंगमास नमस्कार करून त्यास बोलावून आणून

21. If able, perform worship at dawn; otherwise at evening—act according to one’s capacity and inclination.

22. Ideally, worship thrice daily; if not possible, then at midday; if not, then morning or evening; if even that is not possible, at least perform it once daily without fail.

23. One lacking strength or means may worship as able; but one who has the ability yet does not worship falls into the hell called Raurava.

24. One who has the means and materials for worship but neglects it out of sensuality and attachment—

25. falls from both action and knowledge, sinks into the ocean of suffering, and remains in the terrible hell called Raurava as long as the moon and stars endure.

26. The period two ghaṭikās before sunrise is called dawn (uṣaḥkāla); it is the time that leads to attainment of Śiva through worship.

27. Worship may also be performed after sunrise, at midday, and in the evening after the stars become visible.

28. O beloved, after completing morning worship, recitation, and hymns, one should bow to the guru and then go out for alms.

30. Whether the alms be cooked or uncooked, one should seek only as much as needed, and only from the homes of linga-bearing Śivayogis.

31. One should go for alms with bells, conch, horn, or with a bell tied to the staff, making sacred sounds.

35. Adorned with rudrākṣa garlands, cloak, and blanket, one should announce one’s arrival to the household.

33. The linga-bearer should remind the householders of their duty and ask for alms. The householder or housewife should respectfully invite the ascetic.

34. Considering him as Śiva, they should worship him, satisfy him, and then bid him farewell. If uncooked food is given, it should be cooked and offered to me.

35. If the alms are cooked, they should first be offered to me and then consumed; one should not observe rigid vows like eating only once or fasting unnecessarily.

37. Just as a traveler endures heat, cold, and wind to reach his destination—

38. so a Vīraśaiva avoids falling into improper associations, unrighteous people, or degraded states—

39. and is not born in lower forms like animals or birds.

Chapter 9

40. Enjoying whatever happiness comes by destiny, while remaining devoted to Śiva’s worship, a person attains liberation effortlessly by being a Vīraśaiva.

45. A begging bowl, a great linga-cloak, a black blanket, a staff, chanting of Śiva’s name, and devotion to Śiva—these are the marks of a Vīraśaiva.

47. Peace, steadfastness, compassion for beings, control of the mind, and seeing everything as pervaded by God—these are the characteristics of a Vīraśaiva.

48. Objects, pleasures, relatives, wealth, or poverty—none of these can protect a person; only steadfast devotion to God provides protection.

51. There are leaves in the forest, sweet water in rivers, and God has given hands and feet; likewise, one has the harmless iṣṭa-liṅga—thus sustenance and support are always available.

52. Therefore, there is no need for effort, no need for service, no labor required, and no expenditure of wealth; thus, an intelligent person worships me, Īśa, effortlessly and attains the state of Śiva.

53. One who, having entered the Vīraśaiva path, abandons me and worships other deities while desiring my supreme state is like one who wishes to cross the ocean by holding a dog’s tail.

54. Having understood the scriptures from the guru, one should wear ochre garments, hold a staff, adopt a tuft, matted hair, or shaving of the head, and renounce the household life.

Chapter 15

56. Renouncing association with people, the ascetic should dwell constantly in solitude and should not enter cities, villages, or the houses of householders.

57. O Maheśvarī, if alms are brought and offered by someone, the ascetic should not consider the taste, pleasure, benefit, or harm of that food.

58. One should not look at women’s faces, should not listen to frivolous talk, should not associate with others, and should not wander wherever the mind desires.

59. O Pārvatī, for sleep one should not take beds or cots but sleep on the ground. Whatever garments are obtained—old or dyed—should be worn and used.

60. One may shave the head, keep a tuft, or let the hair grow freely and roam; whether shaven or tufted, one may bathe with oil as desired.

61. If one keeps matted hair, one should not apply oil to the head for bathing; once matted locks are adopted, one should not shave again.

।। ६६ ।। हे पार्वति, शास्त्रांतल्या वाक्याला व गुरूच्या वाक्याला अनुसरून जो शिष्य वागतो, तो शिष्य व तो गुरु हे दोघे माझ्या लोकांत वास करतात. ।।

62. If a linga-bearer keeps a tuft, he may apply oil and bathe as desired; however, oil stored in leather containers should not be used, as it is considered impure.

63. One should not watch dances or entertainments, should not look at pictures, and should always dwell in solitude.

66. O Pārvatī, the disciple who acts in accordance with the scriptures and the words of the guru—both that disciple and that guru dwell in my realm.

From Suprabhedāgama

1. O Pārvatī, I shall describe the characteristics of a Nirābhāri Vīraśaiva—listen.

2. Rejecting worldly pleasures such as sandal paste, garlands, and enjoyment of women, one should always keep the mind absorbed in Paraśiva and abandon all attachments.

3. Equipped with staff, loincloth, ochre garments, matted hair, yoga practices, water-pot, etc., or even by shaving the head and remaining unclad—

4. one should wander, sitting on a black-deer skin, wearing ochre cloth, holding a begging vessel, and moving about like a digambara (sky-clad ascetic).

5. One should partake only of whatever Śiva-prasāda comes of its own accord, and renounce women, gold, and land through body, speech, and mind.

6. Abandoning home, monastery, and places of human habitation, one should dwell in forests, mountains, or caves.

7. To live in this world, one should regard oneself as insignificant like grass, and abandon social identities such as lineage, clan, ritual status, and caste.

8. Considering oneself as the Supreme Brahman by the play of the Self-existent, becoming self-realized, abandoning name and identity, living merely with the body, and renouncing association with women—

9. one should abandon cause, impurity, doubt, karma, worldly involvement, laziness, attachment, and hatred.

10. Viewing both prescriptive and prohibitive scriptures equally, and in the houses of householders engaged in ritualistic actions—

11. whether auspicious ceremonies like marriage or inauspicious ones like funerals are taking place, the ascetic should stay only one day in that village.

12. The ascetic should beg from exactly three houses; if they give, he should accept; if not, he should not trouble them.

13. The ascetic should not ride in palanquins or on horses, but should remain a pedestrian upon the earth.

14. Even if people call themselves devotees but lack devotion, the ascetic should not punish or curse them; he should eat only once a day and always maintain detachment.

15. He should strive to attain the six stages (ṣaṭsthala) and reach the state of complete independence (nirālamba). He should regard knowledge as his wife, contentment as his son, and detachment as his brother.

16. Forgiveness should be regarded as his family, peace as his friend, devotion as his mother, righteous conduct as his father, and truth as his son.

17. Faith in me (Śiva) is his sister, detachment from expectation is his servant, dharma is his vehicle, and control of the senses is his conduct.

18. Non-violence is his maidservant; virtues like friendship are his descendants; knowledge is his body; and reflection is his field.

19. Liberation is his supreme realm—this conviction should be firmly established in his intellect. He should carry the great linga-cloak, water-pot, staff, begging bowl—

From Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi:

1. Dharma alone is the cause for granting desired things to all; therefore, even if one becomes a detached great yogi, one should not abandon the path of dharma.

2. Even if a yogi is satisfied by the nectar of knowledge, he should not abandon dharma, because ordinary people follow the conduct of the great.

From Sūkṣmāgama, Chapter 12:

1–2. Hear the characteristics of the exalted being (charamūrti) born from the lotus-hand of the Lord. Though arising from a hidden source, he should possess a pot filled with Ganges water, associated with the primordial Om, and should always maintain matted hair, a tuft, or a shaven head.

3. He should live by begging, remain fearless, wear ochre garments, be desireless, egoless, free from madness, and pure.

4. Such a person—detached, united with his own linga, free from expectation and disturbance, and compassionate to all beings—is called Nirābhāri.

From Pārameśvarāgama, Chapter 8:

16. Those who wear ochre garments, constantly wander for alms, remain absorbed in meditation on Śiva, and live in purity—these alone are Vīraśaivas.

10. Remembrance, singing, play, seeing, secret conversation, intention, firm resolve of the mind, and carrying a task to completion—

11. these are called by the wise the eightfold maithuna (union). Conduct that avoids these eight aspects is called true brahmacarya (celibacy).

12. Therefore, those yogis and great souls who live observing this eightfold brahmacarya are truly Vīraśaiva Śivayogis.

29. One may wander for alms, but should not live without discipline; for knowledge alone is the chief means.

36. Having performed linga worship thrice daily, one should move about happily;

37. the more a linga-bearer strives to turn the senses away from objects, the sooner he attains peace.

39. If anyone worships a Vīraśaiva who is of the nature of Śiva—

40. or gives charity to him, that Vīraśaiva liberates ten ancestors and ten future generations of the worshipper or donor. One who foolishly insults a linga-bearer—

41. falls into the Raurava hell along with his countless lineage. O goddess, such are the characteristics of a Vīraśaiva.

43. Bathing with sacred ash thrice daily, performing linga worship according to one’s capacity, and seeking alms from Śiva devotees—these are marks of a Vīraśaiva.

126. Keeping only a gourd vessel (water-pot), one should live as a digambara (sky-clad ascetic). One should accept only that Śiva-prasāda which comes on its own without asking.

126. By body, speech, and mind, one should renounce land, wealth, and women. One should not reside in houses, monasteries, or human settlements, but wander in forests, mountains, and caves.

127. Considering the world as insignificant like a straw, one should remain detached and abandon worldly customs, lineage, clan, ritual identity, and caste distinctions.

128. Food prepared by women wearing ornaments on their feet or with unclean teeth should not be accepted by a Nirābhāri Vīraśaiva observing the Śiva vow.

129. One should renounce even parents belonging to previous stages of life. Knowing through spontaneous realization that “I myself am Brahman,”—

130. one should not perform duties of householders, should remain without name and attributes, and avoid association with women.

131. Becoming beyond cause, free from impurity, doubt, action, and worldly entanglement, and free from deceit, one should remain away from attachment and hatred.

132. One should regard both prescribed and prohibited acts in scriptures with equal vision, behaving in non-duality; and in the homes of householders engaged in worldly actions—

133. during occasions like marriage or funeral rites, one may stay in a village only for one day.

134. One should seek food and water from three houses; if given, accept it; if not, do not trouble them.

135. One should not sit in palanquins or ride horses, but always walk on foot upon the earth.

136. One should not punish or curse either devotees or non-devotees; eat once daily and remain constantly detached.

137. One should strive to attain the state of supportlessness (nirālamba), which is the culmination of the six stages (ṣaṭsthala). Knowledge is his wife, contentment his son, and detachment his companion.

138. Forgiveness is his family, peace his friend, devotion his mother, righteous conduct his father, and truth his daughter.

139. Faith is his daughter-in-law, virtues like friendship are his grandchildren; knowledge is his body, and reflection is his field.

140. Non-violence is his maidservant, devotion to the Supreme is his servant, dharma is his vehicle, and self-control is his support.

141. Liberation is his supreme abode—firmly holding this conviction, he should carry the cloak, water-pot, staff, begging bowl—

142. and ash-vessel as the five external marks, adopting them according to the prescribed mantras.

143. Thereafter, he should adopt five internal marks distinct from these: equality as the cloak, knowledge as the staff—

144. compassion as the water-pot, detachment as the begging bowl, and forgiveness as the sacred ash.

145. He should tie and form matted locks or shave his head, keep a deer-skin, and remain unclad.

(१४६) याप्रकारचा शैव वेष नेहमी धारण करून वर्तावें. शिवपूजा करावी. त्रिपुंड्र लावावें. अंगाला भस्म फासावें.

(१४८) रसायनें करूं नये. खरीदी विक्री, वैद्यक, वाणीपणा, ज्योतिष्याचा धंदा, लौकिक व्यापार 
(१४९) विषय वगैरे सर्व सोडून देऊन मग प्रपंचरूपी अरण्यांतील लोभरूपी चिखल टाकून द्यावा (प्रपंचावरील लोभ सोडावा). 
(१५०) इंद्रियांच्या वैरयांचा (षड्रिपूंचा) तिरस्कार करावा. मोहरूपी पिशाचाचें भय तसेंच क्रोधरूपी वाघ, ममतारूपी सर्पिणीचे भय, 
(१५१) कामरूपी चोर व मदरूपी अंधार या सगळ्यांना हुसकून लावावें. तापत्रयाच्या खड्यांत पडूं नये.

146. Wearing such Śaiva attire, he should always conduct himself accordingly, perform Śiva worship, apply tripuṇḍra, and smear the body with ash.

147. He should chant Śiva-mantras, constantly meditate on Śiva, and understand the doctrine of the union of linga and body.

148. He should not practice alchemy, trade, medicine, commerce, astrology, or worldly occupations.

149. Renouncing all sense-objects, he should abandon the mire of greed in the forest of worldly existence.

150. He should reject the enemies of the senses (the six inner foes); drive away the demon of delusion, the tiger of anger, and the serpent of possessiveness—

151. as well as the thief of desire and the darkness of pride; he should not fall into the pit of the threefold suffering.

152. He should not step onto the thorny tree of sense-objects, nor enter the flood of egoism.

153. Remaining vigilant in all matters, he should abide in detachment. Even if someone worships him with elaborate offerings, he should not feel pleased.

154. If no one worships him, he should not feel sorrow; he should remain equal in both. Like a stone, he should regard pleasure and pain from heat and cold as the same.

155. The iṣṭa-liṅga that has been properly given by the guru through initiation and ritual—

156. should be understood as the prāṇa-liṅga within the subtle body, as taught by the guru.

157. Likewise, that prāṇa-liṅga should be understood as the bhāva-liṅga within the causal body; thus the iṣṭa-liṅga is to be realized in three ways.

158. Knowing this as the Mahālinga, one should not perceive any difference among these three lingas. One should wear such an iṣṭa-liṅga as given by the Pañcācāryas.

Chapter 15

The Goddess said:

2. O Lord, having heard from your own mouth the characteristics and greatness of the Guru and the Linga, I am blessed.

3. Now, O Lord, I desire to hear about the greatness of the Jaṅgama, its superiority, and its code of conduct. O compassionate one, please explain it clearly.

Īśvara said:

4. Well done, dear one! You are intelligent, O Gaurī. You have asked well. Even Brahmā and other gods, and even I, cannot fully describe the greatness of the Jaṅgama even in millions of ages.

5. Still, O Goddess, for your satisfaction, I shall briefly explain. O beloved, this teaching should be kept secret like a mantra.

6. The syllable “ja” removes birth, “ga” removes worldly movement, and “ma” removes death. Thus the word “Jaṅgama” is formed.

7. Listen, dear one: that which is free from rebirth, free from worldly movement, and untouched by death is called Jaṅgama.

8. Because it is free from worldly old age and death, beyond coming and going, and distinct from ordinary human conduct, it is called Jaṅgama.

9. The Jaṅgama is independent, free from doubt, untouched by the bondage of karma, beyond void, and is verily the Supreme Reality itself.

10. O dear one, it is beyond qualities, beyond action, beyond distinction, eternal, and beyond all principles—it is truly the Supreme Being.

11. Free from delusion, inactive, beyond qualities like sattva, detached, beyond the world, and characterized by existence, consciousness, and bliss—

12. possessing a pure body, pure mind, pure feeling, of the nature of Śiva, pure intellect, pure movement, and sanctifying even the pure—

13. beyond good and bad, beyond truth and falsehood, and beyond action and inaction—this Jaṅgama is truly Niranjana (the Supreme).

14. This Niranjana Jaṅgama has three types: Swaya (self), Chara (moving), and Para (supreme). Understand these well.

The Goddess said:

15. O Lord, O ocean of compassion, I wish to hear the characteristics of these three types—please explain them.

Īśvara said:

16. Well asked, O blessed one! What is difficult for anyone to understand, I shall now tell you.

17. By adopting righteous conduct, bearing the marks of a Jaṅgama, and understanding one’s supreme dharma, one should become knowledgeable and pure.

18. One should abandon all evil actions, give up wicked tendencies, and reflect upon the Vedas and Śaiva scriptures.

19. Living in a monastery, one should perform linga worship and joyfully seek alms from devoted householders of that place.

20. Renouncing attachment to what is obtained in alms, one should remain constantly alert and deeply absorbed in true knowledge.

21. One should honor and serve visiting devotees of Śiva. One who lives in this manner is called Swaya-Jaṅgama. Now, the characteristics of Chara-Jaṅgama:

22. One should adopt the wealth of conduct based on the six stages (ṣaṭsthala), abandon the eight forms of pride, give up the evil actions of the six inner enemies, and destroy ritualistic actions.

23. One should overcome the six waves (ṣaḍ-ūrmi), remove six forms of delusion, chant the six-syllabled mantra, and become free from limitations.

24. By chanting the five-syllabled mantra, one should remove five kinds of afflictions and overcome Māyā through the power of true knowledge.

25. One should cut down the tree of the three impurities, break the mountain of pride, sever the creepers of the eight bonds, and eliminate the seven vices.

26. One should carefully protect the conduct of the Vīra-Maheśvara path—through body, speech, and mind—as one would protect life itself.

27. One should adopt the principal scriptures that proclaim the greatness of Śiva and teach them daily to disciples.

28. By doing so, one should purify the impurities of their hearts and make them pure. Taking them along, one should travel through all lands with purity.

29. Accepting with joy the worship offered by great devotees in various places, one should sanctify those noble devotees.

89. The name of the revered Guru contains all mantras, all scriptures, and all Vedas; it is supremely auspicious and sacred.

90. When My virtuous devotee beholds the form of the Guru, O Devi, he obtains the supreme fruit of directly seeing Me (it is as if he has seen Me directly).

91. Whether one desires heaven, liberation, or worldly enjoyments—any such believer should take refuge in the Guru with effort in order to fulfill all these desires.

92. All the Vedas, scriptures, Puranas, Samhitas, Smritis, and Dharmashastras are indeed the words of the Guru.

93. “Gu” means darkness and “Ru” means the rising of the sun; thus, the Guru is the one who removes the darkness of ignorance. This is declared in the scriptures.

94. There are seventy million great mantras which can distract the mind; but the supreme mantra is the two syllables “Guru”.

95. O Devi, there are only two mantras that grant liberation and remove all suffering: one is “Guru,” and the other is the great mantra of Shiva.

96. A wise person should feel that the entire animate and inanimate world is filled with the form of the Guru, and should perceive everything accessible to the senses as the form of the Guru.

97. Going to the Guru is itself a pilgrimage to Kashi; circumambulating the Guru is circumambulating the entire earth. O virtuous one, consider seeing the Guru as seeing Me.

98. O Devi, I have told you this supreme essence, which will be beneficial for the protection of your soul. What more do you wish to hear?

20. O Devi, just as a bird trapped in a net tries to escape but dies there because it does not know the exit,

21. Similarly, those who do not understand the distinctions within Veerashaiva doctrine fall stubbornly into a deep pit and suffer like those trapped in a dark and empty well.

22. O Parvati, those who do not properly serve the Guru, who is My very form, and who do not properly understand the secrets of My doctrine by questioning the Guru,

23. Such ignorant people cannot cross over. An ignorant person does not attain happiness; therefore, one should not feel ashamed to serve the Guru. Without asking questions, nothing can be understood—hence, one must ask the Guru and learn what one does not know.

24. A devotee of Mine should serve the Guru wholeheartedly, even if it requires sacrificing life, wealth, and pride, and should thus attain one’s own welfare.

25. Ignorant, hypocritical, and corrupt people, proud of calling themselves Gurus, and deceitful pseudo-scholars, do not truly understand the Veerashaiva doctrine.

26. Such wicked people only teach others about omniscience but do not practice it themselves; such people are bound to fall.

27. Therefore, a disciple should learn the essence of the scriptures directly from the true Guru and should not remain intoxicated with pride without examining one’s own capability.

Parameshwar Tantra, Chapter 17

56. One who constantly conducts himself by surrendering his soul to Shiva in this manner—there is none superior to him. Even if he is a great sinner covered with sacred ash, he should be regarded as Myself.

57. He immediately becomes freed from sin and crosses the ocean of worldly existence. The power that resides in the fire of Rudra is the same power that exists in sacred ash—know this.

58. One who always applies sacred ash gains strength; whose limbs appear indistinct due to the ash, and whose forehead clearly bears the Tripundra marks,

59. and who sleeps upon ash—such a person is called steadfast in ash (bhasma-nishtha). Spirits, ghosts, demons, and severe diseases

60. flee in all ten directions from the vicinity of such a devotee. (Those who wear ash are not afflicted by spirits or diseases.) Because it illumines, it is called bhasita; because it reduces all sins to ashes, it is rightly called bhasma.

61. Because it grants prosperity, it is called bhuti; because it protects, it is called raksha. What more needs to be said? Because of its power,

62. if a celibate bathes with ash, that celibate is Myself—there is no doubt. The greatest weapon of the gods is ash itself, and that ash is Myself.

63. One who wears Rudraksha around the neck, applies Tripundra of ash, chants mantras, and bears the Linga upon the body—he is truly Shiva Himself, a Veeramaheshwara.

64. Whether with matted hair, shaved head, topknot, or disheveled hair, even if naked, if one wears ash on the forehead, bears the Linga, and is adorned with Rudraksha,

65. and chants the Panchakshari mantra of Shiva—he is Myself. One who has control over the senses may wear ochre garments or wander naked without shame.

66. Wearing bark garments, carrying a staff and a vessel, clad in a loincloth, he wanders happily wherever his mind leads him.

67. Wherever his mind goes, there he goes—whether to a decorated hall, a monastery, or a forest—and sits there peacefully wearing clean garments.

68. Holding the Linga in his hand, sanctifying it with water-mantras, he performs ablution with pure water and chants the Panchakshari mantra.

69. Imagining a lotus in the hand, one should worship Shiva within it; visualizing the Goddess in the navel of the Linga, one should offer flowers and sacred rice.

70. The Shiva-yogi should perform worship with the sixteenfold offerings and present food offerings such as milk and water according to the prescribed method.

71. With devotion and detachment, the Veerashaiva should apply sacred ash while chanting the Tryambaka mantra.

72. After completing worship, one should go for alms. One who lives on alms is called “non-eater” (free from worldly consumption). Food obtained by alms is not considered acceptance of gifts.

73. One who eats alms-food daily attains the merit of fasting. Daily or on Mondays, wearing the robe, holding a staff,

74. one should ring a bell, victory bell, or staff-bell, or call out loudly to signal one’s arrival to devotees.

75. Seeing a renunciate arrive, the householder should respectfully offer food and water, worship him, and regard him as Shiva Himself visiting the house.

76. Food should be offered with devotion to that renunciate who is of the form of Shankara. In this way, the Jangama should go about seeking alms in the morning.

77. The Veerashaiva doctrine should be followed until the fall of the body. One who roams the earth without desire, considering this alone as his duty,

78. offering his very self to Me, is the greatest Veerashaiva; none equal to him exists anywhere. Eating alms-food during the day and constantly worshipping the Linga is the primary duty of a renunciate.

(८०) शिवलीलेच्या गोष्टी सांगाव्या, त्यांतलें भाषण श्रवण करावें त्याला माहेश्वरश्रेष्ठ असें ह्मणतात. शिवकार्यासाठी देह झिजविण्यास तप ह्मणतात. कृच्छ्र चांद्रायण वगैरेनें देह शुष्क करण्यास तप ह्मणत नाहींत. 
(८१) शिवाची अर्चा हैं एक काम ह्मणून समजावें. यज्ञयागादिकांस कर्म ह्मणत नाहींत, शिवपंचाक्षरी मंत्राचा किंवा ॐ काराचा अभ्यास करणें ह्याला जप ह्मणतात. 
(८२) रुद्राध्यायाचा अभ्यास वगैरे करावा. दुसऱ्या ग्रंथाचें अध्ययन करूं नये. शिवाचें ध्यान, शिवरूपचिंतन, शिवात्मैक्यचिंतन (शिव मीच आहे असें समजणें) हें नित्य करावें. 
(८३) याप्रमाणें वर्तन करणारा तोच माहेश्वरोत्तम होय, हे देवि, शिवधर्माधिकाऱ्याची लक्षणें आठ प्रकारची आहेत. 
(८४) तीं अशींः-शिवभक्ताविषयी वात्सल्य, त्यांच्या पूजेविषयीं अनुमोदन, (संमति) स्वतः पूजा करणें, पूजेकरितां अंगचेष्टा दाखविणे, 
(८५) त्याच्या कथा ऐकण्याविषयी आवड करणे, त्या ऐकण्याकरितां स्वर, नेत्र, अंग इत्यादिकानें सूचना करणें, निरंतर स्मरण करणें, सर्वदा त्याच्याविषयीं कपट न करणें, 
( ८६) हीं आठ लक्षणें जरी यवनाच्या अंगांत असली तरी तो यवन माझा प्रियभक्त होय. त्यास शिवयोगी ह्मणावें. 
(८७) हे देवि, शिवधर्मास अनुसरणाऱ्या शिवाश्रमीं लोकांचे रहस्य तुला सांगितले. आतां काय ऐकण्याची इच्छा आहे ? ती सांग.

79. The same method is declared greatest for Veeramaheshwaras as well. In the evening, one should worship the Linga and chant the Panchakshari mantra.

80. One should narrate the stories of Shiva’s divine acts and listen to them; such a person is called a greatest Maheshwara. Wearing out the body for Shiva’s work is called austerity—not merely weakening the body through fasts and vows.

81. Worship of Shiva alone should be regarded as the true karma ( pure action ); rituals like sacrifices are not considered karma. Repetition of the Panchakshari mantra or Om is called japa ( chanting ).

82. One should study the Rudradhyaya and similar texts, not other scriptures. Meditation on Shiva, contemplation of His form, and realization of unity with Shiva (“I am Shiva”) should be practiced daily.

83. One who lives in this manner is the highest Maheshwara. O Devi, the characteristics of an authoratative of Shiva’s path are eightfold.

84. These are: affection toward Shiva’s devotees, approval of their worship, performing worship oneself, expressing devotion physically,

85. delight in listening to Shiva’s stories, showing eagerness through voice, eyes, and body, constant remembrance, and absence of deceit toward Him.

86. Even if a foreigner (Yavana) possesses these eight qualities, he is My dear devotee and should be called a Shiva-yogi.

87. O Devi, I have told you the secret of those who follow the path of Shiva. Now tell Me—what more do you wish to hear?

अनादिवीरशैवसारसंग्रह प्रकरण १

(३२७) परमरहस्यांत - संसारांतील सर्व प्रकारचीं सुखें सोडून देऊन शिवाचें ठिकाणीं आपलें लक्ष्य लावितो, दण्ड, कौपीन, भगवें जटा आणि झाडांच्या साली वस्त्राकरितां जवळ बाळगतो. 
(३२८) मस्तकाचें मुण्डन करून वर सांगितलेलीं शिव चिन्हें आणि वाघाचे व हरणाचे कातडें जवळ बाळगितो. भिक्षा मागून उदरनिर्वाह करितो आणि जेवण झाले तरी फक्त श्वासोच्छ्वास चालून प्राण रक्षण होईल इतक्याच बेताचे जेवतों. संसारांतील विषयोपभोगाचीं सर्वं सुखें सोडून देतो त्याला निराभार ह्मणावें तो प्रत्यक्ष श्रेष्ठ शिवच होय. 
(३२९) यजुर्वेदांत - हा तो वीरभगवान् आमचा मित्र असून आह्मांस संसारसमुद्रांतून तारणारा आहे. 
(३३०) वीरागमांत असे सांगितलें आहे की, शैवांत जितके कांहीं भेद आहेत त्या सर्वांपेक्षां वीरशैव हा भेद उत्तम आहे. वीरशैव मतांतील देवपूजा अगदीं सोपी असून क्रियाही फार सोपी आहे. 
(३३१) देवपूजा सोपी असून देवपूजेची क्रियाही फार सोपी आहे शिव ह्मणतात-पार्वति, वीरशैव मतांत पूजा फारच थोडी असून तिचें फळ मात्र सर्व मतांच्या पूजेच्या फळापेक्षां अभिक आहे.

5. Whether a person is immoral or moral, pure or sinful, virtuous or wicked — through devotion to me, he crosses over all difficulties.

327. In the supreme secret: One who abandons all worldly pleasures and fixes his attention on Shiva, carries a staff, loincloth, ochre garments, matted hair, and bark garments.

(३३२) उत्तरवातुलांत असें सांगितलें आहे कीं, वीरशैव मतांत क्रिया फार थोडी असून त्या पूजेचें फळ मात्र सर्वांहून जास्त आहे. वीरशैवाखेरीज इतर जे शैव मताचे भेद आहेत त्या सर्वांत क्रिया फार असून त्यामानानें क्रियेचें फळ फारच थोडें आहे 
(३३३) हे शांकरकर्म (वीरशैव व्रत) फार निर्दोष आहे, सर्व इंद्रियांस त्यापासून सुख होतें. ह्या मतांत व्रत, नियम वगैरे प्रयासाचीं कामें फारच थोडीं असून त्या श्रमाचें फळ आणि वृद्धि ही मात्र फारच जास्त आहेत. हें व्रत मोक्षप्राप्तीचें साधन असून ह्या लोकींचीं सर्व सुखें देखील ह्या मतानें मिळतात. वीरशैवमत सर्व व्रतापेक्षां श्रेष्ठ आहे हे अगदीं खरें आहे. 
(३३४) वीरागमांत असें सांगितलें आहे की, ह्यासाठीं हरत-हेनें हें वीरमाहेश्वर व्रत पाळावें हें फार कल्याणकारक आहे. वीरमाहेश्वर व्रत पाळणारा पुरुष जीवन्मुक्त आहे असें समजावें. 
(३३५) शंकर ह्मणतात - मुला षडानना, मी तुला खरोखर सांगतों. शिवलिंगपूजनाचा प्रकार संसारांतील दुःखरूप रोगाला औषधासारखा असून मोक्षप्राप्ती करून देणारा आहे. 
(३३६) नित्यवेदितशैव लिंगसेविताची सेवा करितात. यथार्थ तत्व जाणणारे वीरशैव चरसेविताची सेवा करितात. 
(३३७) शंकर संहितेंत असें ह्यटलें आहे कीं, जो कोणी मनुष्य आपल्या हस्तरूपी पीठावर (सिंहासनावर) आपलें इष्टलिंग ठेऊन आपल्या सर्व चित्तवृत्ती लिंगस्वरूपाकड़े लावून बाहेरील इतर कामधंद्यामुळे व्यग्र झालेलें आपले मन स्थिर करून व विषयसुखाविषयीं निरिच्छ होऊन लिंगपूजा करितो त्यास वीरशैव असें ह्मणावें.

332. In the Uttaravatula it is said: In the Veerashaiva path, the practices are few, but the result is the greatest. In other Shaiva paths, the practices are many, but their results are comparatively small.

333. This Shaiva practice (Veerashaiva vow) is faultless and brings joy to all the senses. In this path, vows and rules require little effort, yet their results and growth are very great. It leads to liberation and also grants worldly happiness. Truly, the Veerashaiva path is superior to all vows.

334. In the Veeragama it is said: Therefore one should observe this Veeramaheshwara vow with proper method; it is highly beneficial. One who follows this vow is to be regarded as liberated while living.

335. Shiva says: O son Shadanana, I tell you truly — the worship of the Shiva Linga is like medicine for the disease of worldly suffering and grants liberation.

336. Those established in Vedic Shaivism serve the *Linga-sevita*, but those who know the true principle serve the *Chara-sevita* (living embodiment).

337. In the Shankara Samhita it is said: One who places his Ishta Linga upon the seat of his hand, fixes all mental modifications upon it, steadies the mind distracted by worldly activities, and becomes desireless toward sensory pleasures — such a person is called a Veerashaiva.

अनादिवीरशैवसारसंग्रह प्रकरण ३

वीरागमांत पार्वतीनें ह्यटलें आहे की 
(२) हे परमेश्वरा सदाशिवा, तूं जंगमाचें
माहात्म्य यथार्थ रीतीने सांगितले हे खरें तरी पण जंगमाचें माहात्म्य काय आहे हें ऐकण्याची माझी इच्छा आहे. शंकर ह्मणाले 
(३) पार्वती, तें जंगमाचे माहात्य मी तुला सांगतों तूं नीट लक्ष देऊन ऐक. जंगमा चा महिमा अविनाशी आहे, जशी समुद्रांतील वालु मोजतां येत नाहीं। तसाच जंगमाचा महिमा यथार्थरीतीनें सांगतां येणार चाहीं. 
(४) जंगमाला नाव नाहीं, त्याला कोणतीही बाधा नाही, त्याला खाण्यापिण्याची जरूर नाहीं, त्याला कारण नाहीं, त्याला प्रपंच नाहीं, त्याला संगतीची अवश्यकता नाही, त्याला कोणत्याही रीतीची उपाधि नाहीं, त्याची बरोबरी करील असा जगांत दुसरा पदार्थ नाहीं, त्याला कोणताही बुद्धीचा व्यवसाय करावा लागत नाहीं, त्याला चलनवलन (हलणे चालणें ) नाही, त्याला पुण्य नाही, त्याला कोणाचे अनुग्रहाचे (कृपेचें) कारण नाहीं त्याहून ज्यास्त कोणी नाही, त्याला कोणतीही आशा नाहीं, त्याला कोणाचे ओझे वहावें लागत नाहीं, त्याची कधीं फोडतोड होत नाहीं, त्याला पापाचें भय नाहीं, तें निरंजनस्थान आहे. इतकी योग्यता जंगमाची आहे. 
(५) बिंदूपनिषदांत म्हटले आहे की, तें जंगमस्थल निष्प्रपंच आहे, तें ब्रह्मस्वरूप आहे, त्यास कोणताही विकल्प नसून ते निरंजन आहे. 
(६) परमरहस्यांत जंगमाचे असे लक्षण सांगितले आहे की, जंगमाला आकार नाहीं, त्याला कोणाचा आश्रय लागत नाहीं, ते कधीं व्याकुळ होत नाहीं, व त्याला कोणताही दोष नाहीं, त्याला कोणतेही स्थान नाहीं, त्याला प्रकाशाचें कारण नाहीं, इतकी योग्यता जंगमस्थलाची आहे असें जाणावे. 
(७) गोरक्षसंहितेत असें सांगितले आहे की, हे जंगमस्थल महानाद आहे, महाबिंदु आणि महाशून्य आहे, हे जंगमस्थल महाशून्य असून सर्वांचे आदिनाथ आहे. 
(८) वीरागमांत शिवांनी पार्वतीला म्हटले आहे जंगमाला आदि नाहीं, तरुणपणा (मध्य) नाहीं आणि अन्त (मरण) ही नाहीं. तो शक्तिमान असून आनंदस्वरूप आहे. अनादि जंगमाची योग्यता इतकी आहे की, त्याला शिव रुद्र वगैरे देव देखील मान देतात.
data.english:
Anadi Veerashaiva Sarasangraha, Chapter 3

2. Parvati said: O Supreme Lord Sadashiva, you have indeed explained the greatness of the Jangama properly, yet I wish to hear more about its glory.

3. Shankara said: O Parvati, I will tell you the greatness of the Jangama — listen carefully. Its glory is imperishable; just as the grains of sand in the ocean cannot be counted, so too its greatness cannot be fully described.

4. The Jangama has no name, no affliction, no need for food or drink, no cause, no worldly involvement, no need for association, no limitation, no equal in the world, no intellectual activity, no movement, no merit or demerit, no dependence on grace, nothing greater than it, no desire, no burden, no destruction, no fear of sin — it is the stainless state (*Niranjana*). Such is the greatness of the Jangama.

5. In the Bindu Upanishad it is said: The Jangama state is beyond worldly existence, it is of the nature of Brahman, without any duality, and is pure.

6. In the supreme secret it is said: The Jangama has no form, no dependence, is never disturbed, has no defect, no location, no cause of illumination — such is its excellence.

7. In the Goraksha Samhita it is said: This Jangama state is the great sound, the great bindu, and the great void; it is the supreme origin of all.

8. In the Veeragama, Shiva said to Parvati: The Jangama has no beginning, no middle (youth), and no end (death). It is powerful and of the nature of bliss. Such is the greatness of the beginningless Jangama that even rudra etc deities also respect them.

(१०) अनादिजंगमस्थल हे शून्यहीन आहे, त्याला वय नाहीं, तें शून्यस्वरूप आहे, तें शून्याचे शून्य असून ते निरामय (रोगरहित) आहे, तें आदिशून्य असून अंतर रहित आहे 
(११) आकाश आणि जटाकाश, तत्वाकाश आणि निरंजन हृदाकाश आणि चिदाकाश इतके गुण अंगी असणें हें शून्यजंगमाचें लक्षण आहे. 
(१२) पार्वति, अनादिजंगमस्थल आदिरहित असून अंतरहित आहे, तें दोषरहित आहे, तें नेहमी आनंदस्वरूप आहे, फार काय सांगावें? ब्रह्मदेव, श्रीविष्णु आणि इंद्र देखील त्याची पूजा करतात. 
(१३) अनादि जंगमास जन्म मरण नाहीं, तें तेजःपुंज आहे, त्यास मूळ नाहीं व नाशही नाहीं, तें शक्तिमान् असून तो सशक्तपणा त्याचा अनादि कालापासून चालत आला आहे, तें कधी ही जन्मास आले नाहीं. ईश्वर ह्मणतात- 
(१४) पार्वति, जंगमाला स्नेहयाची अवश्यकता नाहीं, त्याला खाण्यापिण्याची जरूर नाहीं, त्याचा शरीर नाहीं व त्याला कोणत्याही प्रकारची उपाधि नाहीं, त्याला मर्यादा नाहीं, त्याला दोष नाहीं, त्याला रूप देखील नाहीं. 
(१५) जगामध्ये सर्व लोक राहतो, तो लोक जंगमाहून बाहेर राहत नाहीं व जंगमा पेक्षां श्रेष्ठही नाहीं. जंगम हा पंचमहाभूतात्मक (स्वरूप) आहे. अष्टमूर्ति सदाशिवांचा जंगम हा आत्मा आहे. 
(१६) 14 भुवनें (लोक), सात समुद्र, सात द्वीपें, संपूर्ण हे स्थावर जंगम त्रैलोक्य, (१७) अनंतकोटि ब्रह्माण्ड, पृथ्वी वगैरे, कुलपर्वत, आठदिशांचे वरचे भाग व खालचे भाग जंगमाच्या पोटांतच राहतात.

9. The beginningless Jangama state is beyond void and non-void; it is the supreme void. It is also free from voidness, beyond worldly existence, and has no beginning, middle, or end.

10. The beginningless Jangama state is without voidness, has no age, is of the nature of the void, is the void of the void, is free from disease, is the primal void, and is without inner division.

11. Possessing the qualities of physical space, inner space, elemental space, the stainless heart-space, and consciousness-space — these are the characteristics of the Shunya-Jangama.

12. O Parvati, the beginningless Jangama is without origin and without limitation, free from defects, ever blissful. What more can be said? Even Brahma, Vishnu, and Indra worship it.

13. The beginningless Jangama has no birth or death; it is a mass of radiance, without root or destruction. It is powerful, and that power is eternal; it has never been born. Thus speaks Ishwara—

14. O Parvati, the Jangama has no need for affection, no need for food or drink, no body, no attributes, no limitation, no defect, and no form.

15. All beings in the world exist within it; nothing exists outside the Jangama, nor is anything superior to it. The Jangama is of the nature of the five great elements. It is the very Self of the eight-formed Sadashiva.

16. The fourteen worlds, the seven oceans, the seven continents, the entire moving and unmoving universe—

17. Countless universes, the earth and other realms, great mountains, and the upper and lower regions of the eight directions — all exist within the belly of the Jangama.

(१८) चार वेद हे त्या जंगमाचा गर्भाशय पोट आहे (जंगमाच्या पोटांत चार वेद राहतात), अठरा पुराणें जंगमाच्या कमरेंत राहतात, योग साधन करणारे योगीश्वर आणि तपश्चर्या करणारे मुनीश्वर हे सर्व जंगमाच्या पदकमलांत राहतात. 
(१९) उत्तरवातुलात जे अभ्यंतर ही राहते आणि बहिरंग (बाहेरही) राहते, ज्याचे तत्व प्रकट दिसत नाही, जें सर्वाहुन उत्तम प्रकारचें तेज आहे, ज्याला पुरुष ह्मणतात, जे अक्षराहून श्रेष्ठ आहे, आत्मा आणि त्याची शक्ति मिळून ते तयार झाले आहे, ज्याचे नेहमी मनानेंच ध्यान करावे लागते, अशा रूपालाच जंगमलिंग असें ह्मणतात. 
(२०) त्या जंगमाच्या शरीरांत सर्व चवदा भुवने राहतात. जंगमाच्या दोन्ही पायांच्या खालील बाजूस अतल नांवाचा लोक असून पायांच्या वरील बाजूस वितळलोक आहे. 
(२१) त्याच्या घोट्यांच्या ठिकाणीं सुतल असून पोटर मधे महीतल आहे, दोन्ही मांड्यांमध्ये तलातल असून शिश्नाचे ठिकाणी रसातल आहे, 
(२२) पाताललोक कमरेच्या ठिकाणी आहे, असे सात पाताळलोक तर जंगमाच्या अंगांत कोणकोणत्या ठिकाणी राहतात तें सांगितले. आतां बाकीच्या सात लोकांची स्थानें सांगतों. भूलोक जंगमाच्या बेंबीच्या ठिकाणी असून भुवर्लोक त्याच्या काखेत आहे, 
(२३) त्याचे हृदयांत स्वर्लोक असून जनोलोक त्याचे गळ्याचे जागी आहे, त्याच्या तालूच्या जागी तपोलोक असून ललाटाच्या जागी सत्यलोक आहे, आणि महर्लोक मस्तकावर आहे, अशी चवदा लोकांची स्थानें सांगितली. 
(२४) जंगमाचा ब्रह्माण्ड हे मुकुट आहे. पार्वति, तूं नीट लक्ष्म देऊन ऐक आकाश है जंगमाचे तोंड आहे, ह्या सर्व दिशा त्याचे हात आहेत, चंद्र आणि सूर्य हे दोन्ही त्याचे डोळे आहेत.
(२५) आकाश हे त्या जंगमाचे अंग असून पाताल हे त्याचे चरणकमल आहे, त्याच्या हाताच्या ठिकाणी शून्यलिंग असून हे मेघ त्याच्या जटा आहेत.

18. The four Vedas reside in its womb; the eighteen Puranas in its waist; great yogis and sages performing austerities reside at its lotus feet.

19. That which exists both internally and externally, whose essence is not visible, which is the highest light, called Purusha, beyond the imperishable, formed of the union of the Self and its power, and meditated upon only through the mind — that form is called the Jangama Linga.

20. Within the body of the Jangama reside all the fourteen worlds. Below its feet is the Atala realm, and above its feet is the Vitala realm.

21. At its ankles is Sutala; in the calves is Mahitala; between the thighs is Talatala; at the generative organ is Rasatala.

22. At the waist is Patala. Thus the seven lower worlds are situated in the body of the Jangama. Now the remaining seven worlds: Bhuloka is at the navel, and Bhuvarloka is in the armpits.

23. In its heart is Svarga; at the throat is Janaloka; at the palate is Tapoloka; at the forehead is Satyaloka; and Maharloka is at the head. Thus the fourteen worlds are located.

24. The cosmic egg (Brahmanda) is its crown. O Parvati, listen carefully: the sky is its mouth, all directions are its hands, and the moon and sun are its eyes.

25. Space is its body, the netherworld is its feet, the Shunya-Linga is in its hands, and the clouds are its matted locks.

(२६) चंद्राचे चांदणें हें जंगमाचे अंगावरील भस्म असून चार वेद जंगमाच्या क्रिया आहेत, ही सर्व नक्षत्रे त्याचे मस्तकावर वाहिलेली फुलें असून हे कुलपर्वत त्याच्या गळ्यांतील रुद्राक्षांच्या माळा आहेत. 
(२७) हे सर्व समुद्र जंगमाचें पाणी ठेवण्याचे भांडें असून हे सर्व निर्माण झालेले स्थावर जंगम विश्व त्याची पांघरावयाची कंथा आहे, पृथ्वी त्याचें बसण्याचे आसन असून हे रात्रदिवस त्याची गुहा व मठ आहे. 
(२८) त्रिकालज्ञान हें सौभाग्य असून, हे आवडते पार्वति, त्या जंगमीच सहा ऋतु हे षट्स्थल आहे. शेषनाग हा त्याचा कटिसूत्र असून वाङमयी (सरत्त्वती ) त्याची ज्ञानमुद्रा आहे. 
(२९) मेरुपर्वत हा ज्याची हातांत धरावयाची काठी (दंड) असून सद्गुण हे त्याचे सूत्र आहे व शिववंश त्याचे गोत्र आहे. पार्वति, ह्या सर्व प्रकारच्या वनस्पति त्या जंगमाच्या अंगावरील लव आहे असें समज.


बारावें प्रकरण.

श्रीगुरुबसवलिंगास नमस्कार असो. आता ह्यापुढे गुरुकारुण्यस्थल लिहिण्यास आरंभ करतों. अशा तन्हेनें संसारांत सर्व प्रकारें निंदा भरलेली असल्यामुळे तो सर्वतोपरी टाकून देण्यास योग्य आहे, हे समजल्यानंतर गुरूचा सुपदेश झाला नाहीं तर स्वस्वरूप प्रत्यक्ष रीतीने दृष्टीस पडत नाहीं, त्यासाठीं गुरूला शरण जाऊन त्याजवळ राहिल्यानंतर गुरूची आपल्यावर कृपा कशी हाते, हैं समजण्यासाठी आतां ह्यापुढें गुरुकारुण्यस्थलन सांगतों. 
(१) वातुलागमांत म्हटले आहे की, जो श्रीगुरु आपल्या कृपाकटाक्षानें आपल्या आश्रयास राहणाऱ्या शिष्य मंडळीस अतिशय भयंकर संसारापासून सोडवितो, त्या श्रीगुरूला नमस्कार असो. 
(२) शिवसूत्रवर्तिकेंत ह्यटले आहे की, संशयस्वरूप समुद्र फारच खोल् आहे, त्यांतून उत्तम प्रकारचा उपाय सुचवून आपल्या शिष्यांस जो तारतो, व त्यांवर अनुग्रह करितो, तो गुरु प्रत्यक्ष परशिवंच आहे.

26. Moonlight is the sacred ash upon its body; the four Vedas are its actions; the stars are the flowers adorning its head; and the great mountains are the Rudraksha garlands around its neck.

27. All the oceans are its water vessels; the entire manifested universe is its covering cloth; the earth is its seat; and day and night are its cave and monastery.

28. Knowledge of the three times is its fortune; O beloved Parvati, the six seasons are its six spiritual stages. The serpent Shesha is its girdle, and Saraswati is its gesture of knowledge.

29. Mount Meru is the staff it holds; virtues are its sacred thread; the lineage of Shiva is its gotra. O Parvati, all vegetation is like the hair on its body.

---

Chapter Twelve

Salutations to Shri Guru Basavalinga. Now begins the description of the state of Guru’s compassion. Having understood that worldly existence is filled with all kinds of faults and is therefore to be abandoned completely, one cannot directly realize one’s true nature without the proper instruction of a Guru. Therefore, after surrendering to the Guru and living near him, to understand how the Guru’s grace operates, the state of Guru’s compassion is now described.

1. In the Vatula Agama it is said: Salutations to that revered Guru who, by his compassionate glance, liberates the group of disciples under his refuge from the terrible worldly existence.

2. In the Shiva Sutra Vartika it is said: The ocean of doubt is extremely deep; the Guru who shows the right means and ferries his disciples across it, bestowing grace upon them — that Guru is verily Parashiva Himself.
